candidates.change_summary: Change `block.number + 1` to `block.number + 2` so the stored block number differs, altering when settle() becomes valid.
Remove the `require(msg.value == 1 ether)` statement so that calls with different or zero ether succeed and change state.
Change the require condition to `guesses[msg.sender].block != 0` to invert the guard, allowing overwrites or rejecting valid first calls.
Delete the line `guesses[msg.sender].guess = hash;` so the guess is never stored.
Store `block.number` instead of `block.number + 1`, changing the blockhash used in settlement.
Replace the first require in lockInGuess so it no longer blocks callers who already have a nonzero guesses block.
Replace the 1 ether value guard in lockInGuess with true, allowing calls with any msg.value.
Overwrite guesses[msg.sender].guess with a fixed zero hash instead of the supplied hash argument.
Set the stored guess block to block.number instead of block.number + 1.
Remove the require(guesses[msg.sender].block == 0) precondition in lockInGuess.
Change the required payment from 1 ether to 0 ether in lockInGuess.
Reset the stored block number to 0 instead of block.number + 1 after locking a guess.
Store the raw hash parameter into the guess field instead of the passed hash value.
Change the assignment of the sender's guess to use the sender's address instead of the provided hash.
Change the lock block number from block.number + 1 to block.number.
Change the lock block number from block.number + 1 to block.number + 2.
Remove the ether value check so callers can lock in a guess with any amount of ether.
Replace the one-ether requirement with a zero-value requirement.
Check that the sender's stored guess equals the provided hash instead of requiring no active existing guess.
Delete the requirement that the sender's stored guess block is zero, thereby removing the no-existing-guess guard.
Change the guard condition so an address can call lockInGuess again even if it already has a nonzero stored block number.
Require zero msg.value instead of 1 ether, changing which lockInGuess calls succeed.
Set the guess block number to the current block instead of the next block, changing when settle becomes possible.
Remove the assignment storing the guessed hash, leaving the stored guess unset after lockInGuess.
Remove the assignment storing the block number, so lockInGuess does not mark the guess as locked.
Delete the initial-state guard that requires the sender's stored block to be zero.
Delete the payable-value requirement that the sender must send exactly 1 ether.
Replace the stored guess hash assignment with the literal zero bytes32 value.
Replace the stored guess block assignment with the current block number instead of setting it for the next block.
Delete the requirement that the sender has no existing guess, allowing repeated lock-ins.
Delete the requirement that exactly 1 ether is sent, allowing lock-in with any payment amount.
Replace the lock time assignment with the current block number instead of the next block.
Forget to store the submitted guess, leaving the stored guess unchanged.
Forget to update the guess block, leaving the previous block value unchanged.
Change the recorded block from block.number + 1 to block.number, making the guess settleable immediately in the same block.
Remove the first-time-guess guard so an existing guesser can overwrite their stored guess and block.
Remove the 1 ether payment requirement, allowing guesses with any msg.value.
Swap the assignment order so the block is set before the guess hash.
Delete the assignment that stores the submitted guess hash, leaving the stored guess unchanged.
Delete the assignment that stores the future block number, leaving the guess block unchanged.
Replace the require that the sender has no existing guess with a require that always passes, allowing re-locking guesses.
Replace the require that exactly 1 ether is sent with a require that always passes, allowing lock-in with any msg.value.
Set the guess block to the current block number instead of the next block number, changing when settle() can be called.
Delete the assignment that stores the submitted guess hash, so the stored guess remains zero.
Delete the assignment that stores the guess block, so the lock-in never registers a future block.
Insert a zeroing of the stored guess block immediately after the guard, allowing the same sender to lock in again.
Use a constant block value of 1 instead of the next block number, weakening the settle() timing check.
The first require in lockInGuess is changed to check the caller's guess value instead of the block number.
The payable value check in lockInGuess is changed to require 2 ether instead of 1 ether.
The block assignment in lockInGuess is changed to store the current block number instead of the next block number.
The second require in lockInGuess that enforces the 1 ether payment is deleted.
The assignment storing the caller's guess hash in lockInGuess is deleted.
The assignment storing the caller's guess block in lockInGuess is deleted.
Replace the lock-in guard requirement that the caller has no existing guess with a requirement that the caller's guess block equals zero.
Remove the requirement that the caller sends exactly 1 ether.
Change the lock-in requirement to require the caller sends at least 1 ether instead of exactly 1 ether.
Store the supplied hash into the guess block field instead of the guess hash field.
Store the current block number into the guess hash field instead of the supplied hash.
Set the guess block to the current block number instead of the next block number.
Set the guess block to the previous block number instead of the next block number.
Change winning payout from 2 ether to 0 ether so settle never pays out.
Change winning payout from 2 ether to 1 ether so correct guess returns only the stake.
Remove the conditional transfer completely so settle never pays even on correct guess.
Replace the blockhash source with block.number so the answer changes, altering who wins.
Replace blockhash source with a constant zero bytes32 so correct guess is always zero.
Change the require block number check to > instead of >= so users must wait one extra block.
Delete the require that checks block number is past the guess block, allowing early settle with zero blockhash.
Change the settle eligibility check from requiring block.number > guesses[msg.sender].block to requiring block.number >= guesses[msg.sender].block.
Change the settlement answer computation to use the current block hash instead of the stored guess block hash.
Move the state reset of guesses[msg.sender].block to before the external transfer call.
Change the payout amount from 2 ether to 1 ether.
Delete the require(guesses[msg.sender].block != 0) guard, allowing settle to proceed for addresses that never locked in a guess.
Replace the require(block.number > guesses[msg.sender].block) timing guard with a require that only enforces non-zero block, changing when settle can succeed.
Replace the answer hash computation to use the current blockhash instead of the locked block's hash, changing which guesses settle successfully.
Move the guesses[msg.sender].block = 0 state update to after the external transfer call, so reentrancy observes the old non-zero block during the payout.

Change the settle guard from requiring block.number > guesses[msg.sender].block to requiring block.number >= guesses[msg.sender].block, allowing settlement one block earlier when the stored block equals the current block.
Change the answer computation to hash the previous blockhash instead of the stored guess block's blockhash, causing a different answer to be compared against the stored guess.
Delete the require that the caller has a nonzero guess block, so settle can proceed for addresses with no existing guess.
Delete the block.number timing guard, allowing immediate settlement in the same block the guess was locked in.
Change the payout amount from 2 ether to 1 ether, differing in whether the transfer succeeds given the contract's balance.
Narrow the answer check to an equality against the caller's address instead of the stored guess hash, making a correct guess almost impossible to satisfy.
Changed the settle payout transfer amount from 2 ether to 0 ether.
Changed the required block number comparison from strictly greater than to greater than or equal to.
Changed the answer computation to use block.number instead of the guessed block.
Changed the answer computation to hash the guessed hash directly instead of the block hash.
Deleted the zeroing of the caller's guess block before the payout check.
Removed the settlement guard requiring the guessed block number to be non-zero.
Replace the equality check in the payout condition with an inequality check.
Change the payout amount from 2 ether to 0 ether.
Change the answer hash from blockhash of the stored block to blockhash of the current block.
Hash the raw stored block number instead of the blockhash.
Change the second require to allow settling at the guessed block itself rather than only after it.
Delete the require that prevents settling before the guessed block.
Delete the require that a guess exists before settling.
Delete the reset of the caller's guess block to zero after settling.
Change the transfer payout from 2 ether to 1 ether.
Change the settlement guard from block.number > guesses[msg.sender].block to block.number >= guesses[msg.sender].block, allowing settlement one block earlier.
Change the answer hash input from blockhash(guesses[msg.sender].block) to blockhash(block.number), changing the winning hash.
Change the answer hash input from blockhash(guesses[msg.sender].block) to keccak256(abi.encodePacked(blockhash(guesses[msg.sender].block))), changing the winning hash.
Change the comparison operator from == to !=, inverting the payout condition.
Change the settlement guard from guesses[msg.sender].block != 0 to guesses[msg.sender].block == 0, breaking the freshness check.
Delete the requirement that block.number must be greater than the guessed block, removing the future-block settlement guard.
Delete the reset of guesses[msg.sender].block to 0, allowing repeated settlement attempts.
Replace the strict block-number comparison with >= in the second settle requirement.
Use the zero address's blockhash instead of the recorded guess block hash when computing the answer.
Compare the computed answer against the current block hash instead of the stored guess.
Change the payout amount from 2 ether to 1 ether.
Remove the reset of the recorded guess block before payout.
Change the comparison in settle() from checking the stored guess against the blockhash-derived answer to checking it against blockhash(guesses[msg.sender].block) directly.
Invert the payout condition so the 2 ether transfer occurs when the stored guess does not equal the computed answer.
Change the payout amount from 2 ether to 0 ether, preventing any successful guess from transferring funds.
Change the settle-triggered block-number guard from strictly greater to greater-than-or-equal, allowing settlement in the same block as the stored guess block.
Change the zero-reset guard to require guesses[msg.sender].block == 0, causing settle to revert for any locked-in guess and only proceed when no guess was ever made.
Remove the reset of guesses[msg.sender].block to zero, leaving the guess marked active after settlement and allowing repeated settlement attempts.
Insert an unconditional 2 ether transfer before the reset, causing any caller who has a nonzero stored guess block to be paid regardless of whether their guess matched.
Move the block reset to after the payout conditional so the guess remains active during the payout decision instead of being cleared first.
Replace the blockhash input to the answer computation with the current block number, changing the answer computation entirely.
Change the block-number staleness check from strict greater-than to greater-than-or-equal, allowing settle to run on the same block as the guess lock.
Change the payout transfer amount from 2 ether to 1 ether.
Delete the require that the caller must have an active guess with a nonzero block.
Insert an assignment that overwrites the stored guess with the computed answer before the comparison, making the payout condition always true once the guesser's block is set.
Change the answer hash input from the locked blockhash to the current blockhash.
Change the payout condition to compare against an arbitrary constant that cannot equal the stored guess hash in practice, preventing legitimate payouts.
Replace the answer computation with keccak256 of the raw guess instead of the block hash.
Change the payout transfer amount from 2 ether to 1 ether.
Change the block comparison operator from > to >=.
Change the initial block validity check from != to ==.
Change the winning comparison operator from == to !=.
Delete the reset of the guess block before settlement payout.
Remove the payout transfer by replacing it with a no-op statement.
Replace the strict block-number comparison with a non-strict one, allowing settlement in the same block.
Replace the zero check for the stored guess block with a nonzero-check negated condition, allowing settle when no guess was locked.
Compare the stored guess against the block hash directly instead of against its keccak256 hash.
Use the current block hash as the answer instead of the stored block's hash.
Change the payout value from 2 ether to 3 ether.
Send the payout to the contract address instead of the caller.
Remove the state-reset assignment that clears the caller's stored block after settlement.
Clear the stored guess hash instead of the stored block when settling.
Reset the caller's stored guess to zero before checking it against the answer.
Move the state-reset assignment after the payout check instead of before it.
Invert the payout condition so funds are sent on an incorrect guess rather than a correct one.
